title: Lesson 2: Where AI Already Creates Value in an Org (and Where It Does Not)
description: Grounded in Lesson 2 of the AI Adoption series: where AI reliably produces value, the readiness tests that identify value-ready work, and why redesigning the workflow matters more than the tool.

questions.question: Which profile of work is the strongest candidate for AI?
options: Rare, high-stakes decisions where an error is expensive and hard to detect
Open-ended creative work that has no objective standard of quality
High-volume work with repeatable inputs and cheap-to-check output
Work whose output nobody can name until the project is finished
questions.explanation: Value concentrates in work that is high volume, has predictable inputs, produces a clear output, and can be checked cheaply with errors that are easy to fix.

questions.question: Two organizations buy the same AI tool and get very different results. What best explains the gap?
options: One bought a more capable model and paid a higher license price
One redesigned the workflow around the tool instead of bolting it on
One gave the tool to a much larger number of employees across several teams
One ran a longer training program before the launch
questions.explanation: Value is a property of the redesigned workflow, not of the model, so the same tool performs differently depending on whether the work around it changed.

questions.question: Which condition most reliably makes AI a poor fit for a piece of work?
options: The task repeats often and a reviewer can verify its output quickly
The task has structured inputs with predictable fields
The team is willing to change how the work gets done
A wrong answer would be hard to detect and expensive to undo
questions.explanation: When an error is hard to spot and costly to reverse, a confident wrong answer does more damage than no answer at all.
